stage: S2/S4 shared-ledger implementation diagnostic,not Earth calibration or production adoption
question: Can finite requested services consume only an explicitly uncommitted staff-hour budget supported by the same settlement food ledger,across multiple request types?
parents: Preserve active r44 physics,source/context studies and current Earth-atlas settlement scenarios exactly. Source-composition a9b3858c supports separate observation/demand channels,not direct role/authority assignment.
primitive: Take existing destination-choice request allocations for multiple channels. At each provider,sum requested hours across ALL channels,then apply a common proportional fulfilment factor min(1,available hours/requested hours). Keep unreachable and capacity-unmet requests explicit. This is single-pass proportional rationing,not maximum flow,rerouting,queues,prices or an equilibrium. Spare capacity elsewhere may coexist with unmet requests.
labour_adapter: Use supported institutional_people already inside SettlementPlan.total_people and its periodic food-year check. Gross staff-hours = those same people times caller-specified hours per supported staff member. Subtract explicit already-committed hours BEFORE service allocation;reject overspending or unsupported/malformed plans. Return used and remaining hours. No implicit creation of staff,food or extra residents,or reuse of the full budget separately per channel.
integration_diagnostic: Read BOTH current raw/corrected Earth-atlas settled_reach.json.gz snapshots. Exclude unconstrained reference case. For every existing food-constrained case,reconstruct the periodic food check from recorded arrivals,need and stored residents;verify cohort/total/food ceiling and existing needs. Do not refit/reallocate food or modify source atlas files. All marked/proposed sites and actor uncertainty remain unchanged.
illustrative_work_scenarios: Exactly600annual gross hours per already-supported staff member,with0%,50%,100% of that budget explicitly committed to other duties. These are declared stress scenarios,not empirically estimated ancient hours or additional harvest work. Legacy control has no quantified staff-hour claim yet,so none is assumed free by default for production use.
illustrative_requests: Two neutral service channels,A and B,each one potential annual request per SAME recorded total resident. One hour per A request and two hours per B request,arbitrary declared unit scenarios. Identity destination choice at original site tests coupling only;no new travel catchment,market,administration or garrison inference. Every setting retained,no best-case selection.
checks: Test shared-hour competition,unreachable demand,zero capacity,overspend rejection,nonmutation and identity coupling to actual allocate_settlement food support. Hand-computed heterogeneous costs,explicit no-rerouting example and invalid shapes/NaN/negative inputs. Independently recompute every diagnostic case from recorded arrays,verify per-origin request and per-provider hour ledgers,identical old source artifacts and fresh replay.
publication: Aggregate results and a fixed comparison figure on the collapsed Earth research page; model-only per-site arrays may be exported with clear provenance. No raw archaeological observations or new production control/settlement map. Zero total demand yields null coverage,never a perfect score.
limits_and_next: This implements an honest consumer,not calibrated service productivity or qualified roles. Next add dated/source-supported institutional/exchange demand,monthly staffed-provider network access and explicit shared labour commitments for patrol/collection/services.
